narration: The pipeline starts with the first input: a sequence of RGB video frames of a person moving, captured over time.
The second input arrives below it: the matching sequence of pressure maps recorded from the floor over the same time window.
Each modality goes into its own encoder. The image encoder is frozen, marked by the snowflake, while the pressure encoder is trained.
The encoded features then pass through an LSAM block on each branch, which refines the per-modality representation.
Both streams meet in FCAM, the Fusion Cross-Attention Module, where image and pressure information are combined.

Inside FCAM, image features become value and key, pressure features become the query. Query and key are multiplied and softmaxed into attention weights, applied to the value, added back through a residual, passed through a position-wise feed-forward layer, and finally concatenated with the original features.
The fused representation flows into the regressor, which maps it to human body parameters.
The regressor predicts pose parameters theta and global translation T, supervised by the pose loss and the translation loss.
From theta and T, the 3D joint positions J of theta and T are computed and supervised by the 3D loss.
Those 3D joints are then orthographically projected to the image plane, where the 2D loss is applied.
The result is the reconstructed 3D motion sequence, with a contact loss that keeps the predicted body in agreement with the measured foot pressure contacts.
Finally, the legend: the crossed circle is matrix multiplication, the plus is addition, and C is concatenation. That completes the full architecture.
